title: [CQ-R09c] Copy-only snapshot materialization in the guest
description:
Objective: copy one exported source snapshot (protected base plus overlay) into an owned guest's workspace over the protected supervisor's stdin, never a mount. Prove that the guest received exactly those bytes, and that no host filesystem is mounted in the guest before or after the copy.

Context: third slice of CQ-R09 (task-0dd1cce23a6646fd80cf401dd47c7b0f), split 3 ways on 2026-10-27 with the operator's approval in the architect REPL. It builds on the landed CQ-R08 bridge chain and CQ-R10a's teardown in guest-supervisor.py (both DONE). It consumes the SourceSnapshot shape that CQ-R09b (task-697fb2de19324ccb851defaf9f24043b) produces, but its tests build snapshots with validateImport directly, so it runs in parallel with R09b; CQ-R09 final's end-to-end test joins the two. CQ-R09 final adds the export direction on top of this module and mode, CQ-R10 binds attempts to the workspace defined here, and CQ-R11 extends materialization to check environments.

Deliverable:
1. New scripts/local-runner/snapshot-transfer.mjs exporting:
- SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_BYTES = 1048576, the raw bytes per host data frame.
- workspaceEntries(snapshot): checks the SourceSnapshot shape (version 1, sealed base and overlay), then returns validateImport of the merged view: base files, replaced or added by overlay files, minus overlay deletes. Its digest is the materialization identity.
- snapshotArgv(name, mode): frozen ['exec', '--no-map-working-directory', name, '--', 'sudo', '-n', GUEST_LAYOUT.supervisor, mode], for an owned instance name and mode 'materialize' or 'export' only.
- assertNoMounts(name, provider): readGuestInfo must report zero Multipass mounts and the R07 mountinfo probe must show no host-sharing filesystem, reusing guest-readiness.mjs's mount rule (export mountFailure unchanged). Otherwise it throws TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT or TRANSFER_MOUNTS_UNKNOWN; provider failures keep their fixed PROVIDER_* codes.
- runSupervisorStream({ name, mode, provider, timeoutMs, input, onFrame }): spawns snapshotArgv(name, mode) through provider.spawn (default child_process.spawn) with shell:false. It writes the input frame Buffers to stdin with backpressure, then ends stdin; decodes stdout with createFrameDecoder(MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES), calling onFrame with each decoded object; and resolves only after stdout EOF and provider exit 0 within timeoutMs. Any other outcome kills the provider and rejects with a fixed TRANSFER_* code (spawn, timeout, exit or frame), never guest text. An error thrown by onFrame kills the provider and rejects with that same error.
- materializeSnapshot({ name, snapshot, provider = {}, timeoutMs }): assertNoMounts; stream the frames below; require exactly one {kind:'materialized', digest} whose digest equals workspaceEntries(snapshot).digest; assertNoMounts again; then resolve frozen { instance, digest, files, bytes, executionReady: false }.
Host frames, each within MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES: {kind:'snapshot', version: 1, files, bytes, digest}; then, per file in manifest order, {kind:'file', path, executable, size} followed by ceil(size / SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_BYTES) {kind:'data', data} frames of base64; then {kind:'end'}.

2. guest-supervisor.py materialize mode. main(['materialize']) runs only as euid 0 (else 77); any other argv stays 64. materialize(in_fd, out_fd, workspace=WORKSPACE, manifest=WORKSPACE_MANIFEST, owner=None):
- WORKSPACE = '/var/lib/moe/workspace' and WORKSPACE_MANIFEST = '/var/lib/moe/workspace.manifest.json'. An existing workspace or manifest exits EX_CANTCREAT (73).
- It builds the tree in a root-only (0700) staging directory beside WORKSPACE, with directory-fd-relative O_NOFOLLOW and O_EXCL creates. No symlink is ever followed, and a traversal, absolute, empty-segment, NUL or duplicate path is refused even from the host.
- It checks every size and the header counts, and recomputes R09a's digest framing from the bytes it wrote.
- On a match it gives the tree to the AGENT_IDENTITY account (root directory 0700) and renames it into place. It then writes WORKSPACE_MANIFEST (root, 0600, O_EXCL; UTF-8 JSON {"version": 1, "digest": hex, "files": {path: [executable, size, sha256 hex]}}), which CQ-R09's export mode diffs against, writes exactly one {kind:'materialized', digest} frame and exits 0.
- A malformed or out-of-order frame, a bound breach or a mismatch exits EX_DATAERR (65); an I/O failure exits EX_IOERR (74). Both remove the staging tree and write no frame.

3. Tests in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs. Host rows reuse its fakeGuest mount fixtures and a fake spawn. Supervisor rows load the real guest-supervisor.py under python3 -I -B with injected workspace, manifest and owner (the R08b test-seam pattern). One end-to-end row materializes through the real supervisor. Rows that need POSIX python skip on win32 with a reason.

Not in scope: the export/import direction and its supervisor mode (CQ-R09 final); per-attempt workspaces, job identities or credentials (CQ-R10); check environments (CQ-R11); host admission (CQ-R12); real VM certification (CQ-R13); `multipass mount` or `multipass transfer`. executionReady stays false and verified-local stays unavailable.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-snapshot.test.mjs
definitionOfDone: The snapshot reaches the guest only through snapshotArgv(name, 'materialize') on the supervisor's stdin, spawned with shell:false. No mount or transfer subcommand, host path or snapshot byte appears in any provider argv (tests record every provider call).
materializeSnapshot refuses unless readGuestInfo shows zero mounts and mountinfo shows no host-sharing filesystem, both before and after the copy, and it never spawns when the first check fails.

Identities come from the transferred bytes: the supervisor recomputes R09a's digest from the bytes it wrote, and the host accepts only one materialized frame whose digest equals workspaceEntries(snapshot).digest. A wrong, missing or repeated frame, or a nonzero exit, is a fixed refusal.

The materialize mode refuses traversal, absolute, empty-segment and duplicate paths, symlink-redirected writes, and an existing workspace or manifest. After any failure it handles, it leaves neither a staging tree nor a partial workspace (supervisor rows under python3).
The listed verification command exits 0 and its fresh output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
runSupervisorStream and materializeSnapshot in scripts/local-runner/snapshot-transfer.mjs, plus test rows T4-T6.

runSupervisorStream({ name, mode, provider = {}, timeoutMs = 120000, input = [], onFrame }):
- Validate before any spawn, else TRANSFER_INPUT_INVALID:
  - argv = snapshotArgv(name, mode);
  - provider is a plain record. Its optional executable is a non-empty string without control characters (default 'multipass'), and its optional spawn is a function (default child_process.spawn);
  - timeoutMs is a safe integer from 1 to 600000;
  - input is an iterable of Buffers, and onFrame is a function.
- Spawn with spawn(executable, argv, { shell: false, windowsHide: true, stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] }). A throw, or a child without the stream and kill shape, is TRANSFER_SPAWN_FAILED.
- stdin: write the input in order, honouring backpressure (await 'drain' when write returns false), then end it. An EPIPE or stdin error after the child has gone does not crash anything; the exit decides the outcome.
- stdout: decode with createFrameDecoder(MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES) and pass each decoded object to onFrame synchronously. A decoder error is TRANSFER_FRAME_INVALID, and decoder.end() must pass at stdout end.
- stderr is drained and discarded, never buffered.
- Settle exactly once:
  - resolve only when stdout ended cleanly, onFrame never threw, and the child closed with code 0;
  - a nonzero code or a signal is TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED;
  - the deadline is TRANSFER_TIMEOUT;
  - an error thrown by onFrame is rejected as-is;
  - every failure kills the child with SIGKILL, and every path removes listeners and clears the timer.
  Follow guest-session.mjs's single-settle teardown where it fits.

materializeSnapshot({ name, snapshot, provider = {}, timeoutMs }):
1. manifest = workspaceEntries(snapshot). This is pure and runs before any provider call.
2. await assertNoMounts(name, provider).
3. runSupervisorStream with mode 'materialize', input hostFrames(manifest), and an onFrame that accepts exactly one frame: exact keys {kind:'materialized', digest}, with digest === manifest.digest. A wrong digest is TRANSFER_DIGEST_MISMATCH. Any other kind, extra key or second frame is TRANSFER_FRAME_INVALID, and so is no frame once the stream ends.
4. await assertNoMounts(name, provider) again.
5. Resolve Object.freeze({ instance: name, digest, files: manifest.entries.length, bytes: <sum of sizes>, executionReady: false }).

Tests T4-T6 use fakeGuest for run and a spawn-compatible fake made of Node streams, like fakeProvider in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Its kill() emits 'close' asynchronously through setImmediate, as Node does; a synchronous close masks the kill path. Record the spawn arguments and every stdin byte. Build each hostile case so exactly one rule fails.
- T4 A clean materialize resolves the frozen result:
  - the provider calls are exactly info, mountinfo, the spawn of snapshotArgv(name, 'materialize') with { shell: false, windowsHide: true, stdio pipes }, then info and mountinfo;
  - the decoded stdin frames are exactly the header, then file plus data frames per entry, then end. A 2.5 MiB file gives 3 data frames, and an empty file gives none;
  - no frame carries a host path, and no argv carries a snapshot byte.
- T5 Mounts present or unknown before the stream refuse it, with no spawn. Mounts that appear after the stream (a fakeGuest info sequence) give TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT.
- T6 Each of these is a fixed refusal: a wrong digest (TRANSFER_DIGEST_MISMATCH), no frame, two frames, an extra key, an unknown kind, a malformed or oversize guest frame, a nonzero exit, a signal exit, and a hung child with timeoutMs 50. The child is killed whenever the stream did not end cleanly. A direct row shows that a thrown onFrame error surfaces unchanged through runSupervisorStream.

Error handling: settle once, kill on every failure, and no unhandled rejection.
implementationPlan.note:
runSupervisorStream and materializeSnapshot added. A shared streamOptions validates everything before any provider call or spawn, so materializeSnapshot refuses a bad timeoutMs or provider before its first mount check (T5). supervise() spawns snapshotArgv with { shell:false, windowsHide:true, stdio pipes } and settles once. Resolve needs all input written (stdin ended), a clean decoder.end() at stdout EOF, and close code 0. Exit 0 before the input was taken, a nonzero code or a signal gives TRANSFER_EXIT_FAILED; code 0 without a clean EOF gives FRAME_INVALID. A thrown onFrame error rejects unchanged. Every failure destroys stdin and SIGKILLs. feed() awaits 'drain' (or 'close' once torn down), so the stdin queue holds at most one data frame past its high-water mark. Deviation: child listeners are not removed on settle; a settled flag guards them, and the no-op error listeners must stay to absorb a late EPIPE. The timer is cleared on every path. Tests:
- T4: exact provider order, exact decoded frames (2.5 MiB file = 3 data frames, empty file = none), stdin bytes equal to hostFrames, and a backpressure peak bound.
- T5: input refusals with no provider call; mounts before the stream with no spawn; late mounts in info or mountinfo.
- T6: 11 hostile answers with the kill assertion; the guest exiting 0 before it took its input; the direct onFrame throw; runSupervisorStream input and spawn refusals; a non-Buffer input item.
RED: the import SyntaxError before the functions existed. GREEN: T1-T6 pass; the file gives 199 tests, 198 pass, 1 pre-existing skip. Size so far: module 193, readiness +1/-1, tests +184.

implementationPlan.description:
Materialize mode in scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py, plus supervisor rows M1-M4. R10a's relay, GUARD and signal handling stay untouched.

Constants: WORKSPACE = '/var/lib/moe/workspace'; WORKSPACE_MANIFEST = '/var/lib/moe/workspace.manifest.json'; SNAPSHOT_DIGEST_TAG = b'moe-source-snapshot-v1\0'; MAX_SNAPSHOT_FILES = 10000 and MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES = 268435456, mirroring source-snapshot.mjs.

main(): ['materialize'] joins ['bridge'] as the accepted argv, and anything else stays 64. A euid other than 0 gives 77 before stdin is read. At euid 0 it returns materialize(0, 1).

materialize(in_fd, out_fd, workspace=WORKSPACE, manifest=WORKSPACE_MANIFEST, owner=None):
1. owner defaults to the (pw_uid, pw_gid) of pwd.getpwnam(AGENT_IDENTITY); a KeyError gives EX_OSERR (71). If the workspace or the manifest already exists (os.path.lexists), exit EX_CANTCREAT (73) without reading stdin.
2. Create the parent directory if it is missing (root, 0o755). Create the staging directory with tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='.workspace-', dir=parent), which makes it 0700, and open it with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW.
3. Read frames from in_fd with os.read in a loop until EOF, through take_frames(buffer, data, MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES):
   - the first frame must be exactly {kind:'snapshot', version:1, files, bytes, digest}, with files <= MAX_SNAPSHOT_FILES, bytes <= MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES and digest 64 lowercase hex;
   - then, exactly files times, {kind:'file', path, executable, size} followed by {kind:'data', data} frames whose base64.b64decode(data, validate=True) payloads are non-empty and sum to exactly size;
   - then {kind:'end'}, then EOF.
   Keys are exact everywhere. Anything else is EX_DATAERR (65): a running total over the header's bytes, or any byte after end, included.
4. Each path is a str with no NUL, does not start with '/', and has no '', '.' or '..' segment. The host has already applied R09a's rules; this is defence in depth.
   - Walk the parents with os.open(segment, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=...), creating a missing one with os.mkdir(segment, 0o755, dir_fd=...) and opening it the same way.
   - Create the file with os.open(leaf, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o755 if executable else 0o644, dir_fd=...). A duplicate (FileExistsError), or a path under an existing file (NotADirectoryError), is EX_DATAERR.
   - fchown each created directory and file to owner.
   - Write with a full-write loop while hashing, and close every fd on every path.
5. After end:
   - the counts and the total must equal the header's;
   - snapshot_digest(rows) must equal the header digest. It uses R09a's framing over rows of (path.encode('utf-8'), executable, size, raw sha256), sorted by the path bytes: the tag; u32be count; then per entry 0x46, u32be path length, the path, an executable byte (1 or 0), u32be size and the 32 raw sha256 bytes.
   Otherwise exit EX_DATAERR.
6. fchown the staging root to owner, keeping it 0700, then os.rename(staging, workspace). Then write the manifest:
   - os.open(manifest, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600);
   - UTF-8 JSON {"version": 1, "digest": digest, "files": {path: [executable, size, sha256 hex]}}, with ensure_ascii=False, a full-write loop and fsync.
   Then write_frame(out_fd, {'kind': 'materialized', 'digest': digest}) and return 0.
7. Failures:
   - ValueError, KeyError, binascii.Error and frame errors exit EX_DATAERR (65);
   - OSError exits EX_IOERR (74);
   - both remove the staging tree with shutil.rmtree if it still exists, and write no frame;
   - a manifest failure after the rename also removes the workspace it just renamed, so a workspace never exists without its manifest.

Update the header comment with the modes and exit codes 65 and 73. Keep the file stdlib-only, LF and ASCII.

Supervisor rows M1-M4 go in the CQ-R09c section:
- Load the real file with python3 -I -B and importlib: copy LOAD and harness from scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. -B is mandatory, and never add a CLI test mode. Skip on win32 with a reason.
- Feed stdin with hostFrames output for clean rows, and with encodeFrame for hostile rows. owner is the current uid and gid, and the workspace and manifest live under a mkdtemp directory.

Rows:
- M1 CLI surface: ['materialize', 'x'] and ['MATERIALIZE'] give 64 with empty stdout; main(['materialize'], geteuid=lambda: 1000) gives 77 with empty stdout. S7's bridge assertions still pass.
- M2 A clean stream writes exactly the files, with their bytes, owner +x bits, modes 0644/0755 and a 0700 root; the manifest, at 0600 with the exact JSON; and one materialized frame whose digest equals validateImport(...).digest computed in Node. This is the cross-language digest proof.
- M3 Each refused stream gives 65 with empty stdout, and leaves no workspace, manifest or .workspace-* staging directory: '../x', '/abs', 'a//b', a NUL, a duplicate path, 'a' then 'a/b', a wrong digest, a short or long data total, data before a header, a missing end, bytes after end, more files than the header counts, and non-canonical base64.
- M4 An existing workspace, an existing manifest, and a symlink at the workspace path each give 73 and stay untouched. A symlink redirect: monkeypatch os.mkdir in the harness to plant a symlink to an outside temp directory instead of one parent directory. The next O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW open fails, the run exits 65 or 74, nothing is written in the outside directory, and no staging directory is left.

Error handling: every fd closes on every path, and no traceback or path reaches stdout.
implementationPlan.note:
guest-supervisor.py materialize mode (+163/-6). R10a's relay, GUARD, Termination, Bridge and pump are byte-identical. The only shared edit: write_frame now calls a new write_all (the same partial-write loop), which the manifest writer reuses.
- main(): ['materialize'] is accepted next to ['bridge']; anything else is 64; a non-root euid gives 77 before materialize runs; at root it runs materialize(0, 1).
- materialize():
  - owner defaults to the moe-agent pwd entry, with KeyError giving 71; an existing workspace or manifest (lexists, so a symlink counts) gives 73 before stdin is read;
  - makedirs(parent, 0755), then mkdtemp('.workspace-', 0700) beside the workspace, held open with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW;
  - snapshot_frames() reads frames through take_frames with MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES, and a partial frame at EOF is a ValueError;
  - receive(): exact keys everywhere, and type(v) is int, so JSON true is not version 1. Bounds: files <= 10000, bytes <= 256 MiB, each size within the header's remaining total. Each data chunk is non-empty, never past its size, and canonical base64 (decode with validate=True, then re-encode and compare). end, then EOF, with the total spent exactly. The R09a digest is recomputed from the written bytes, sorted by UTF-8 path bytes.
  - create(): path segments are bytes; a NUL or an '', '.' or '..' segment is refused ('/abs' splits to ''). Parents are opened O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW by dir_fd, and a missing one is mkdir'd 0755 and opened the same way. The file is O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW. fchown plus explicit fchmod (0755/0644) on every created node, so the modes do not depend on the umask. EEXIST and ENOTDIR become DATAERR.
  - On a match: fchown the root (kept 0700), rename into place, then write the manifest (O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW 0600, compact UTF-8 JSON, fsync). If the manifest write fails, the renamed workspace is rmtree'd. Then one materialized frame.
  - ValueError/RecursionError give 65 and OSError gives 74; the finally closes root and rmtrees the staging tree.
- Header comment: modes and exit codes 65/73. The file is stdlib-only and ASCII (grep -P finds nothing).

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's diff (load the adversarial-self-review skill). Read it as each attacker in turn:
- A broken or hostile host stream: wrong order, counts or totals; a duplicate path; '..'; a NUL; huge declared sizes; non-canonical base64; bytes after end.
- A crash or SIGKILL mid-materialize: only a root-only .workspace-* staging directory may remain, never a workspace without its manifest.
- A pre-existing workspace, a manifest, or a symlink at either path.
- Two materializations at once on one VM. Document that callers serialize per VM through R06's job lease, and that rename refuses a non-empty target.
- A guest that floods stdout or stderr, never exits, exits nonzero, or answers with the wrong digest.
- Host-side backpressure on a 256 MiB snapshot. Peak memory is the manifest copy plus one chunk; say so in a comment if it is more.
Check that error handling never leaks a path, guest text or byte; that DoD 1-4 each have a test that fails if its guard is removed (spot-check one guard at a time in a git archive scratch copy, never in the shared tree); that R10a's relay is byte-identical; and that verified-local and executionReady are unchanged.
Fix anything found with a test, then re-run step 5's command and supply that fresh output to complete_task.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review findings and fixes:
(1) materialize renamed the staging tree into place before writing the manifest, so a crash between the two left a workspace with no manifest. An fsync failure also left a partial manifest; the RED fsync-injection row left 'workspace.manifest.json' behind. Fix: write_manifest runs first and unlinks its own file on failure; a failed rename unlinks the manifest. The M4 fsync and rename injected-failure rows expect 74 with an empty lib. GREEN.
(2) Mutation sweep, 28 single-guard mutants run in /tmp scratch copies, never the shared tree. The JS mutants were shell:true, mode export, each of the 2 mount checks, digest, second frame, no frame, extra key, code!==0, !fed, kill, drain, decoder.end, base delete. The Python mutants were digest, sort, '..', canonical b64, short total, after-end, staging rmtree, O_NOFOLLOW, lexists, manifest unlink on rename, partial manifest unlink, ENOTDIR, fchmod and main routing. 27/28 were killed at first. The survivor, main's 'materialize' routing as root, got an M1 row (monkeypatched materialize gives 42 and '((0, 1), {})'), so 28/28 are now killed.
Residuals:
- An O_EXCL removal is masked by the digest recompute.
- An empty-snapshot concurrent race (rename onto an empty dir) is excluded by R06's per-VM lease.
- A segment over 255 bytes gives 74, not 65; R09a prevents it on the host.
- Files are not fsynced; the VM is disposable.
- Listeners are guarded by the settled flag and not removed.
- A crash after the manifest write leaves the manifest plus a root-only staging dir, so a retry gives 73 (fail-closed).
No __pycache__, no sleeper processes. The full gate exits 0 (279 tests, 278 pass, 1 skip). T1-T6 pass there, and M1-M4/T7 skip by NOT_POSIX as designed. No __pycache__. Both new runtime files are ASCII and LF.

DoD:
1. T4/T7 record every provider call: info, mountinfo, a single spawn of ['multipass', snapshotArgv(name,'materialize'), {shell:false, windowsHide, pipes}], then info, mountinfo. fakeGuest.unexpected stays [], and the stdin bytes equal hostFrames exactly.
2. T5: mounts present or unknown before the stream mean no spawn, and late mounts in info or mountinfo give TRANSFER_MOUNTS_PRESENT.
3. Supervisor side: the digest is recomputed from the written bytes, and M2/T7 give a cross-language digest equal to Node's (UTF-8 vs UTF-16 order is exercised by U+1F600 and U+FF5E). Host side: T6 refuses a wrong, missing or repeated frame, an extra key, an unknown kind, malformed, oversize and truncated frames, a nonzero or signal exit, a hang, and an early exit 0.
4. M3: 27 hostile streams each give 65 with an empty lib dir. M4: 73 untouched for an existing workspace, manifest or symlink; a planted parent symlink is never followed; injected fsync and rename failures leave nothing.
5. Gate exits 0 (above).

My own mutation sweep (26 single-guard mutants, scratch copies, scored by exit code) killed 24/26:
- JS: shell:true, both mount checks, digest, repeat, fed, kill, no-frame, decoder.end, delete-ignored, backpressure.
- Python: O_NOFOLLOW walk, digest, sort, canonical b64, after-end, rmtree, lexists, '..', fchmod, unlink on rename, root 0700, bool version, manifest-after-rename.

Two survivors, advisory and not blocking. In both, a later check still yields 65, so the outcome is unchanged:
(a) O_EXCL removed from the file create. M3's duplicate row also breaks the digest, so it masks the guard (the worker disclosed this).
(b) The per-file `size <= left_total` bound: the end-of-stream total catches the breach, but only after the bytes are written.

A test that computes the R09a digest over the duplicate rows would pin (a). R10a relay: the only change is write_frame delegating to the new write_all.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) `multipass transfer` or a mount. Rejected: DoD and rails require copy-only transfer with no host filesystem in the guest, and transfer writes as the default user into a path the supervisor would then have to trust.
2) A tar stream extracted by the guest's tar. Rejected: it needs a tar writer on the host and trusts guest tar's extraction rules. Instead the supervisor, a protected root binary already hash-pinned by R07, writes with dir-fd O_NOFOLLOW|O_EXCL creates and recomputes R09a's digest, so the host gets byte-exact proof of receipt.
3) Building in place under an atomic mkdir claim. Rejected: a crash would leave a partial workspace. Staging plus rename leaves at most a root-only staging directory.
4) Making R09c depend on R09b. Rejected: R09c only needs the SourceSnapshot SHAPE, which its tests build with validateImport, so both run in parallel. CQ-R09 final's X7 joins the real exporter with this transfer.
5) Trusting the guest's materialized frame alone. Rejected: the host also re-checks mounts after the copy and accepts exactly one frame with the expected digest.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Landed facts:
- guest-supervisor.py (R08b/c, R10a; 429 lines at plan time):
  - write_frame is the only stdout writer, and take_frames(buffer, data, limit) decodes host frames;
  - exit codes 0/64/71/74/75/76/77/78 are taken, so add 65 (EX_DATAERR) and 73 (EX_CANTCREAT);
  - AGENT_IDENTITY is 'moe-agent', and main() injects geteuid;
  - tests import the file with python3 -I -B and importlib (LOAD and harness in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs). S7 asserts that it is stdlib-only and pins bad-argv exits, and it stays green.
- guest-readiness.mjs: mountFailure(result, {info}) is module-private, so export it unchanged. readGuestInfo and runGuestProbe(name, 'mountinfo') run through provider.run. GUEST_PROBES.mountinfo is ['cat', '/proc/self/mountinfo'].
- guest-bridge.mjs: bridgeArgv is the pattern for snapshotArgv. encodeFrame and createFrameDecoder exist, with MAX_HOST_FRAME_BYTES 4 MiB and MAX_GUEST_FRAME_BYTES 256 KiB.
- guest-session.mjs is the single-settle spawn and teardown template, with stdin-first teardown and SIGKILL on failure.
- local-runner.test.mjs:
  - fakeGuest({info, answers}), whose info accepts an array sequence for 'mounts appear later', plus healthy(), guestDetail(), mountinfo() and MOUNTS, all near line 940;
  - every module is imported statically at the top.
- source-snapshot.mjs: validateImport and the digest framing that the Python mirrors.

The CONTRACT that CQ-R09 final (task-0dd1cce2) plans against. Keep these names and shapes exactly: SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_BYTES, workspaceEntries, snapshotArgv, assertNoMounts, runSupervisorStream (an onFrame throw rejects as-is), materializeSnapshot, transferError codes, and WORKSPACE, WORKSPACE_MANIFEST and the manifest JSON. CQ-R10 and CQ-R11 will build on WORKSPACE.
planningNotes.risks:
- Size: about 490 changed lines are expected: module about 140, Python about 90, tests about 250. The operator approved the split preview at about 450, and an R09c/R09 size-exception rail is proposed (cap 520). Measure early with git diff --numstat; comments and blank lines count.
- Cross-language digest: Python must sort by UTF-8 path bytes, not str order, and frame exactly as source-snapshot.mjs does. M2 compares against Node's validateImport digest.
- fchown as a non-root test user works only to its own uid and gid. Tests inject owner, and production defaults to moe-agent.
- An empty-snapshot workspace is an empty directory, and rename replaces an empty target directory on Linux. Concurrent materialization is excluded by R06's per-VM job lease; document it, no lock file.
- Python 3.12 in the Ubuntu 24.04 guest; CI ubuntu and macos have 3.12+. base64.b64decode(validate=True) refuses non-alphabet characters. Check canonical padding by re-encoding if needed, so the host and guest agree.
- Windows: the supervisor rows and T7 skip on win32 only. T1-T6 use fakes and must pass on windows-latest.
- Hangs and orphans: give async rows timeouts, kill python children in t.after, and run the pgrep check after any mutation sweep (Serena gotcha-local-runner-supervisor-tests).
- Out of scope: the export/import direction (R09 final), per-attempt workspaces, credentials and running jobs (R10), and real VM certification (R13). executionReady and verified-local are unchanged.

completionSummary:
